page.layout: One column of running text; no notes in the margins. Below the text: the catchword at the right and a gathering signature at the left. Show-through from the reverse appears at the foot.

main_text.p: scilicet, eo praesente propter gratiam & autoritatem ejusdem, quam apud multitudinem habebat, minus periculi à motu hujus sibi esse futurum. Nec opinionem populi & spem regum fefellit eventus. Nam cum domum Lycurgus redisset, reperissetque omnes ordines praesentis conditionis suae ac status pigere, & animis pendentes in sese oculos conjicere, prehendendam occasionem se offerentem ratus, cum paucissimis quibus maximè fidebat, communicato consilio ad reformandum regni & reipublicae statum serio animum adjecit. Verum priusquam palam quicquam occiperet, gnarus, religione mentes hominum plurimum moveri, & Minois exemplo, de quo in Creta edoctus erat, permotus, Delphos ad sacra facienda & consulendum Apollinem profectus fuit. Quibus ritè illic peractis, gaudens Spartam repetiit, ferens secum oraculum illud fama celebratum, quo dilectum Diis, aut DEVM potius quàm hominem Pythia sacerdos eum salutavit, & mox εὐνομίαν[?], hoc est, bonarum legum formam & reipublicae ordinationem flagitanti respondit, dare ac polliceri DEVM eam, quae omnium rerumpublicarum futura esset longè praestantissima. Hoc igitur responso magis magisque

page.notes: The Greek word after "mox" is faint; the reading εὐνομίαν is uncertain. Its breathing and accents are not clear. The line "Hoc igitur responso magis magisque" ends the page with the catchword "anima." below. Show-through from the reverse appears at the foot (mirrored letters below the signature) and as small marks in the right margin; these are not printed text and are left out. Paragraph breaks were not clearly visible, so the page is given as one running paragraph continuing from the previous page. The signature "C" at the left foot is faint.
